q: What is the minimum clear width of a hospital corridor used by patients on beds or stretchers?
n: Bed/stretcher corridors: at least 2.44 m (8 ft) clear. Remember this: "6-8 and 4-8." Corridors: 6 ft (1.83 m) for non-patient, 8 ft (2.44 m) for beds. Ramps: 4 ft (1.22 m) one-way, 8 ft (2.44 m) two-way. Slope 1:12, like 12 months to climb 1 year.

q: Corridors NOT commonly used for bed, stretcher and equipment transport may be reduced to what clear width?
n: Non-patient-transport corridors may drop to 1.83 m (6 ft).

q: What is the steepest allowed slope of a hospital ramp?
n: Ramps shall not be steeper than 1:12.

q: What is the minimum clear width of a hospital ramp used in ONE direction?
n: One direction: 1.22 m (4 ft). Two opposite directions: 2.44 m (8 ft).

q: What is the minimum clear width of a hospital ramp serving TWO opposite directions?
n: Two-way ramp = double the one-way width: 2.44 m.

q: If a hospital has upper-floor clinical areas and NO multi-level ramp, what must be provided?
o: An elevator that can carry at least a patient bed
A stair with landings every 10 steps
n: Upper-floor ancillary, clinical and nursing areas need a ramp or elevator; without a ramp, the elevator must fit a patient bed.

q: When is an entry ramp required at a hospital entrance?
o: When the entrance is not on the same level as the ground
Only when there is no elevator
n: Any entrance not at ground level needs an entry ramp.

q: The DOH floor-plan checklists require a ramp for wheelchair access at the Emergency Room with a clear width of at least:
n: Same as the one-way ramp width in Annex B: 1.22 m.

q: The Level 1–3 hospital floor-plan checklists require patient corridors for ingress and egress to be at least how wide?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex H-6a item 2.2.3; H-6b item 2.2.3; H-6c item 2.2.4
n: The checklists repeat the 2.44 m patient corridor rule.

q: Which needs the WIDER clear width under DOH rules?
o: A corridor not used for bed transport
A corridor used for patient beds
n: Bed corridor 2.44 m > non-bed corridor 1.83 m > one-way ramp 1.22 m.

q: A hospital entrance is 0.60 m above the ground. At the DOH maximum slope, what is the minimum horizontal run of the ramp?
A service corridor in the administrative wing is drawn 1.50 m wide. Does it meet the DOH minimum for corridors not used for bed transport?
o: Yes, any width is fine for service corridors
No, it must be at least 1.83 m
No, it must be at least 2.44 m
n: Even the reduced corridor is 1.83 m (6 ft).

q: True or false: A two-way hospital ramp needs 2.44 m clear width.
n: 1.22 m one way, 2.44 m two ways. Remember this: "6-8 and 4-8." Corridors: 6 ft (1.83 m) for non-patient, 8 ft (2.44 m) for beds. Ramps: 4 ft (1.22 m) one-way, 8 ft (2.44 m) two-way. Slope 1:12, like 12 months to climb 1 year.

q: Fill in the blank: Ramp slope shall not be steeper than 1:___.
n: 1:12, the same ratio used in BP 344.

q: Match the width: 1.83 m (6 ft) belongs to which element?
o: Corridor not used for bed or stretcher transport
n: Think "6 ft for walking, 8 ft for wheeling beds."

q: True or false: Without a multi-level ramp, the hospital elevator must accommodate at least a patient bed.
n: Bed-size elevator is the fallback when there is no ramp.
